conflicts.outcome:
The 6 November ruling ranks first and lifts the block. The address book manages transporters: a transporter is a record held per organisation in trade-imports-address-book, in a transporters collection of its own with its own document, controller, repository and route, reusing the service's organisation scoping, soft-delete, locking and Standard Address Block validation, holding no role and storing a private-or-commercial type instead (req-transporters-001 to req-transporters-004). Adding one mid journey uses the address book hand-off already built for addresses rather than a second pattern of its own, so the add pages are the ones the INS front door serves and the animals frontend's three transporter add-page folders come out (req-transporters-005, c-transporters-001). Every row that changes how transporters are listed, searched or added therefore goes ahead: the list's heading, search, columns, 'Not applicable' cell and 'View details' link, the type page's wording, both add forms and what follows a save, the private transporter's country list, the address book's transporter rows and its Transporter tab, and the list's paging (req-transporters-009). Much of it has since landed on the animals frontend and in the address book, so this re-distil records most of those rows as already existing rather than as changes; where the address book's own add pages read differently from the design the difference is its own row (req-transporters-006 to req-transporters-008).
